title: Welcome to Nepal
excerpt: Nepal is one of the richest countries in the world in terms of bio-diversity due to its unique geographical position and latitudinal variation. The elevation of the country ranges from 60m above sea…
content:
Nepal is one of the richest countries in the world in terms of bio-diversity due to its unique geographical position and latitudinal variation. The elevation of the country ranges from 60m above sea level to the highest point on earth, Mt. Everest at 8,848m, all within a distance of 150 km with climatic conditions ranging from sub-tropical to arctic. This wild variation fosters an incredible variety of ecosystems, the greatest mountain range on earth, thick tropical jungles teeming with a wealth of wildlife, thundering rivers, forested hills and frozen valleys.

Within this spectacular geography is also one of the richest cultural landscapes anywhere. The country is a potpourri of ethnic groups and sub-groups who speak over 70 languages and dialects. Nepal offers an astonishing diversity of sightseeing attractions and adventure opportunities found nowhere else on earth. And you can join in the numerous annual festivals that are celebrated throughout the year in traditional style highlighting enduring customs and beliefs.

We welcome you to take part in any of the activities that we offer and we are glad to extend our warm hospitality to make your stay in Nepal a memorable one.

Namaste

 

Please contact us for the following services:

  • Cultural, Adventure & Jungle Safari packages for groups & individuals
  • Sightseeing tours in/an around Kathmandu valley
  • Arrangement for incentive tours
  • Tours to Tibet/China, Bhutan , India and Myanmar
  • Trekking & White Water rafting
  • Hotel reservation
  • Domestic & International ticketing
  • A scenic Mountain Flight
  • Special interest/Cultural Tours
  • And all tourism related services

title: Nepal Information

Nepal is one of the richest countries in the world in terms of bio-diversity due to its unique geographical position and altitudinal variation. The elevation of the country ranges from 60m above sea level to the highest point on earth, Mt. Everest at 8,848 m, all within a distance of 150 km resulting into climatic conditions from Sub-tropical to Arctic.

Nepal – occupying only 0.1% of the total landmass of the earth – is home to:

2% of all the flowering plants in the world;
8% of the world’s population of birds (more than 848 species);
4% of mammals on earth;
11 of the world’s 15 families of butterflies (more than 500 species);
600 indigenous plant families;
319 species of exotic orchids.

 

Nepal at a Glance

 Area  :   147,181 Sq. Km
 Location  :   Situated between China in the north and India in the South, East and West.
 Capital  :   Kathmandu
 Population  :   23.1 Million
 Language  :   Nepali is the national language. However travel-trade people understand and speak English as well.
 Currency  :    Nepalese Rupee (Approximately USD 1 equals Rs. 74.55 as of January 2006).
 Political System  :    Multi-party Democracy with constitutional monarchy.
 Religion  :    Nepal enjoys the distinction of being the only Hindu Kingdom in the world. However, there is harmonious
 blending of Hinduism and Buddhism.
 Climate  :    Nepal has four major seasons, namely: 1. Winter: December-February, 2. Spring: March-May,
 3. Summer: June-August, 4. Autumn: Sep-Nov. Nepal can be visited the whole year round.
 People  :    Nepal has more than 101 ethnic groups and 92 spoken languages.
 What to wear   :    Light weight clothing is recommended for May through October. Warm garments are required in
 October-March. An umbrella or a raincoat is a must for the rainy season.

Adventure Specialist Travel (AST) was started in 1995. The Founder of AST is Mr. Raj K. Shrestha, who began his career in Tourism business in 1988. 19 years in the tourism trade helped him to gain enormous experience in making attractive tour/trek packages and traveled a lot to add realistic/practical knowledge on all the tour packages, he initiated.

He also traveled to Europe  and USA several times to do the marketing and promote Nepal as a tourist destination among his friends, clientele and tour operators. He is multilingual personnel with high ability to understand western as well as eastern cultures. He facilitates westerners to understand Nepali culture properly and motivate them to support Nepal in different ways, either by visiting Nepal as tourists or initiating deference development projects in Nepal, which will help Nepal and Nepalese for a better future.

You can visit following website for more information on his social contributions and development works in Nepal, which he has been doing for more than a decade.

www.nepalhilfe.de
He believes in generating more employment opportunities through tourism and it is one of the biggest foreign currency earners for this country. AST contributes 10% of its earnings to all the development works; he has been involved in the country. Therefore, booking a trek with AST, you can also contribute to our efforts to make our dreams of ‘better Nepal for tomorrow” come true!

www.fwhcnepal.org.np
AST is a registered travel agency under the Ministry of Tourism and Civil Aviation, Tourism Department (Reg. No. 426/053), Ministry of Commerce and Industries (Reg. No. 5990/053/54), Nepal Government, and is an active member of Nepal Association of Tour and Travel Agents (NATTA), Nepal German Chamber of Commerce & Industry (NGCCI) and several other local Associations, which promotes tourism business for Nepal.

Our main office is located at Pulchowk, Lalitpur, exactly at the Gateway to the famous Patan Durbar Square (one of the World Heritage Site), in front of the Municipality Building, Lalitpur, Kathmandu Valley. AST is also affiliated with numerous agencies/companies from all over the world and has an aim to bring many tourists to Nepal in order to generate more job opportunities to youths, who are leaving this country due to lack of proper opportunities in the country. As per recent statistics, it is estimated around 600 to 800 youths, who are leaving this country EVERYDAY for better jobs outside the country. Skilled and talented youths are also attracted to go abroad for better opportunity, which is definitely a ‘brain-drain’ from this country. Therefore, by booking trips with us, you will also help generating job opportunities in Nepal, thus helping Nepal & Nepalese.

Our Administrative staff can deal with all your queries, and there will always be someone in the office to answer your questions regarding trips to this part of the world instantly. All Staff members are qualified to answer your all queries regarding the trip to Nepal as well as trips to Bhutan, Sikkim & Tibet.

Some more reasons, why you choose our Company for trips to this part of the world:

  • We try to make your holidays, a lifetime experience! so that you can have a positive impression of your trips and the areas, you are traveling. AST cares for good services and value your money paid for the services. AST does not compromise with better services. If you would like to have references of our previous customers, who live nearby your hometown or region, AST can provide you for your references and probably even done the same trip, you are considering!
  • Friendly Staff: Nepalese are traditionally friendly people and easygoing people. All staffs, either in the field or in office, are very friendly or care for better hospitality. AST Team consists of the staffs, which come from the northern part of the country, where all high mountains are located, as well as from the lowlands of the country, where people are trained for extreme mountainous activities and have also climbed several high peaks in the country. Staff members are also from the famous trekking areas of Nepal, such as Everest region, Annapurna region, Langtang region, who are eagerly awaiting to take you to their regions to show their life style and let you enjoy the sceneries seen from their home places. Our staffs are well trained to handle high altitude sickness besides their normal safety measures for clients and are very conscious about keeping better environment in the areas, they take you.
  • Hygienic food & water: AST is very concerned about your fooding or eateries in Nepal, when you are traveling here. It tries to suggest you better & hygienic places, where you can go and eat, however, most of the Restaurants, which are meant for tourists, are, of course, better managed, hygienically. While on trek, AST provides plentiful, healthy, wholesome and varied foods, prepared by cooks trained in modern cooking hygiene. Special care is taken to serve well-boiled and purified drinking water everyday, while on the tour or trekking, to ensure that our clients stay healthy and enjoy their outing fully. Our cooks for the trek are famous for their ability to produce varied and tasty meals in adverse conditions.
  • Group Size: AST can organize trips according to the size of the group, which can be from minimum number of participants to high number of participants. AST has organized many trips, which consisted to maximum 8 pax in a group. However, it also organized tour/trek for a group of 30 pax recently in Nepal. AST can prepare varieties of itinerary according to the size of the group. There are also tours on ‘group joining’ basis for those, who are interested and like to do the tour with the people from different countries or even same country!
  • Environmental Concern: AST briefs all the staffs to make them aware of environmental issues in the areas, they take clients and are very much conscious about it. It is more precisely done, especially, when AST has group to a trekking in the country. AST uses kerosene or gas for cooking purpose on the trek to avoid burning firewood. We recycle non-biodegradable waste and use centralized toilet tents. Our staffs are trained in the correct disposal of waste. All biodegradable waste is burned and buried before breaking camp every morning. Non-degradable wastes (tin, cans, bottles, plastic, etc.) are carried back to Kathmandu for proper dispose. Care is also taken to fill in toilet holes after use.
  • Insurance: Every single porter and staff employed by AST for the trek, is not only well paid, but also protected by a life insurance policy.

title: Trekking/Tour Season
excerpt: WHEN TO GO TO NEPAL These are typical weather and trekking conditions you may encounter month by month but remember that every year is different. Conditions vary from one trekking region to another…
content:
WHEN TO GO TO NEPAL
These are typical weather and trekking conditions you may encounter month by month but remember that every year is different. Conditions vary from one trekking region to another and mountains make their own weather - even in traditionally dry months it can rain.

JUNE, JULY & AUGUST: The monsoon is in full swing and these months are not good for trekking, except in Dolpo, Mustang and Tibet, which are in the rain shadow of the Himalayas.

MID – LATE SEPTEMBER: A fair amount of cloud and rainfall still around. Lush vegetation and wildflowers, hot temperatures at low altitudes and a few leeches presents, but pleasant trekking higher up.

OCTOBER & NOVEMBER: Clear skies and good visibility; still warm at lower altitudes but nights could fall to –15C above 4000m. November is cooler than October.

DECEMBER: Great temperatures for trekking below 2500m but can get very cold at night at higher altitudes, with temperatures down to-20 C or colder. With proper clothing, trekking can be very rewarding because of the excellent visibility. Light snowfalls a possibility.

JANUARY: Conditions similar to December, but often colder.

FEBRUARY: Still excellent visibility but starting to warm up during the day, especially later in the month. Good trekking at lower altitudes but still cold at night higher up.

MARCH: Still good visibility and getting warmer at low altitudes Wild flowers and rhododendrons start to bloom and a good month for birds.

APRIL: Rhododendrons in full bloom, alpine flora at higher altitudes and plenty of bird life, hot trekking at lower altitudes but ideal temperatures higher up. More cloud and haze around in the pre-monsoon build up, especially in the afternoons.

MAY: Very hot at lower altitudes but excellent trekking higher up. Abundant flora, especially alpines; mornings often still clear but cloud and haze around and possibly some pre-monsoon showers.

 

EQUIPMENT & CLOTHING:

Equipment needed depends largely upon where, when and how one is trekking. The main emphasis while trekking is on keeping warm and dry while still being lightweight. For lower altitude, fleece jackets and pants are adequate, while at higher altitudes down jackets are advisable. Waterproof, wind-proof jackets and pants, well broken-in footwear, head covering are also recommended. Good sleeping bags, sunglasses, drinking water bottle, torchlight, sun block cream, toiletries, first aid kit and a very good route map are other items necessary. Cameras, on the other hand, are handy for taking home memories.

Trekking equipments are available for hiring in Kathmandu, Pokhara and Namche Bazaar.

 

HEALTH & MEDICINE:

Medication shops are few on trekking routes. Therefore, it is best to carry first aid kit and read about the possible problems before hand. On the Everest Base Camp route at Pheriche and on the Annapurna Circuit route at Manang, there are clinics operated by the Himalayan Rescue Association that specializes in treating trekker’s heath problems. These clinics are open only during the main trekking seasons. While on treks, the following problems could occur:

  1. Upset stomach, often caused by change in diet or contaminated food and water in a common ailment. To avoid it, one should pay particular attention to hygiene and quality of food and drinks.
  2. Cough, cold, sore throats, common in the dry mountain air can lead to chest infection. Sore throats can best be avoided by attempting not to breathe cold air directly through mouth. Smoking should also be avoided.
  3. Joint muscle strains, food problems and blisters are other hindrances for trekkers. Wearing good footwear will go a long way in avoiding these problems. For sprains and strains, apply cold water to reduce swelling and support the joint with crepe bandage.
  4. Acute Mountain sickness (AMS) is a fatal sickness caused by random altitude ascension. Therefore, climbers ascending 3,000 meters or above should acquire sound knowledge of proper acclimatization processes. Symptoms of AMS include headache, loss of appetite, swelling of limbs, dizziness, difficulty in sleeping, irregular breathing, nausea and unusual weariness. Maintaining good fluid intake helps combat altitude sickness and hurried descent or evacuation to lower altitude in the only best cure.

 

SAFETY & SECURITY:

Nepal is a safe country to trek provided the basis rules are observed. When with trekking agency most contingencies are handled by agency staff. However, one could get lost or hurt and have no one to ask for help when trekking alone. Therefore, trekkers should either trek with agencies, or hire reliable guides if trekking in smaller groups. The best way to avoid risk while trekking is through thorough planning, playing by the rules and realizing human limitations. In case of misfortune, a short detailed message should be dispatched to a reliable organization or individual immediately for rescue operation. If communication facilities are unavailable, normal first aid principles should be followed till help arrives. Some of the safety rules to abide by are:

  1. Do not trek alone.
  2. Do not make a display of wealth.
  3. Keep belongings secure and within sight.
  4. Make arrangements for handling emergency situations before hand.
  5. Register personal information and trekking plan details with respective embassies.
  6. Buy travel insurance policy that cover helicopter rescue cost. Leave a copy of details with an agency in Kathmandu.
  7. Choose only authorized government registered travel and trekking agencies, guides and porters.

NATIONAL PARKS AND RESERVES

Royal Chitwan National Park, situated in the inner Terai plains was the first national park of Nepal Tropical forest sand grasslands her contain large populations of the one horned rhino and other endangered species like the Royal Bengal Tiger Gangetic dolpin, gharial crocodile and gaur Bison. 440 species of birds are found in the park, including the giant hornbill, the paradise flycatcher, and the Bengal florican.

 2. Sagarmatha National Park  1148 Sq. kms  North East of Nepal
 3. Langtang National Park  1710 Sq. kms  32 km North, Kathmandu
 4. Royal Bardia National Park  968 Sq. kms  Mid far western Terai
 5. Shey Phokshundo National Park  3555 Sq. kms  Mountain Region of Western Nepal
 6. Rara National Park  106 Sq. kms  371 km from Kathmandu, North West of Nepal
 7. Makalu-Barun National Park  2330 Sq. kms  
 8. Khaptad National Park   968 Sq. kms  
9. Annapurna Sancturary Koshi Tappu Wildlife Reserve  175 Sq. kms  Eastern Nepal
